title: QUIC RFC 9000 Preferred Address Field Shape
purpose: Describe the bounded RFC 9000 Section 18.2 preferred_address transport-parameter field-shape proof and the adjacent server-address cutover hook.
design_summary: The transport-parameter codec encodes preferred_address as a server-only transport parameter whose value always contains the IPv4 address, IPv4 port, IPv6 address, IPv6 port, connection-ID length, connection ID, and stateless reset token fields in RFC 9000 order. IPv4 and IPv6 address bytes are copied in network byte order, ports are two-byte big-endian values, the connection-ID length remains the separate one-byte field owned by ARC-QUIC-RFC9000-0031, and the stateless reset token is preserved as the final 16 bytes associated with the preferred-address connection ID. The runtime cutover proof for S18P2-0019 uses the existing preferred-address path-validation flow: a received preferred-address candidate remains pending until validation succeeds, then the active server address changes to the preferred path and the preferred-address connection ID becomes the current peer destination connection ID.
data_and_state_considerations: The preferred_address codec stores IPv4 and IPv6 address fields as byte arrays and ports as UInt16 values. All-zero address-family values remain explicit fields rather than omitted fields. Runtime preferred-address state is still committed through peer transport parameters and is not promoted until path validation completes.
edge_cases_and_constraints: A preferred_address that omits the unused all-zero address family is rejected because both address families and ports remain required fields.
Truncated preferred_address values are rejected before parser state is committed.
IPv4 and IPv6 address fields retain exact network-byte-order bytes.
IPv4 and IPv6 ports are preserved as two-byte big-endian fields.
The stateless reset token remains exactly 16 bytes at the end of the preferred_address value.
Preferred-address runtime cutover remains validation-gated and does not broaden the full S9.6 migration lifecycle.
risks: This slice is focused field-shape and bounded runtime cutover proof; it does not claim the existing preferred-address connection-ID constraint lane.
This slice does not claim public migration APIs, multipath behavior, or hosted interop readiness.
This slice relies on the existing transport-parameter benchmark scenarios that already include preferred_address parse and format coverage.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes the selected S18P2 preferred_address field-shape family and a bounded S18P2 pointer to preferred-address server-address cutover. It does not reopen connection-ID sequence/accounting constraints under ARC-QUIC-RFC9000-0031 or disable_active_migration behavior under ARC-QUIC-RFC9000-0062.
